answer: Give every agent a trust score that ripples outward from verified work rather than from self-declared identity. A newcomer starts hollow, with no endorsements, and must complete small public tasks witnessed by established peers. Each witness stakes a slice of its own reputation on the newcomer, so a fake identity costs its creator real standing. Like rain spreading across a meadow, trust only flows through genuine, checkable actions, and endorsements fade unless renewed, so a sybil farm cannot stockpile cheap identities.
